note: Inscribed Indus objects found in sources checked in this project that are NOT in the merged corpus. Readings are sign identifications by rendering comparison (Wells numbers), not interpretations.

objects.source: Hulínek & Hulínková Ťuchová (eds) 2018, Preliminary Report Archaeological project SAHI - Tell Jokha, 2017 (Season 2), Bratislava, pp. 59 and fig. 6.61 (p. 183 of the PDF); photo data/images/tell-jokha-TJ17-PRO-S56.jpg
objects.object: fragment of a square stamp seal (signs incised, i.e. the seal itself); photo published upside down
objects.field_symbol: part of an animal, ribbed/pleated neck (probably unicorn)
objects.confidence: 740 (jar, M342) certain; 803 = M387 (oval with trident) confirmed against Mahadevan 1977 sign list p. 35; preceding signs lost

Salut-ST1-jar-impression.object: local jar (body sherd + rim sherd, same vessel?) stamped twice before firing with an elongated seal
Salut-ST1-jar-impression.reading_note: Signs faint; photo shows an oval-with-chevron (opener W861/817 family) and a box sign; excavators call it 'almost identical' to Mohenjo-daro seal M-1367 (merged corpus: SEAL:R Scene, seq [362, 861]). Our own look at the photo is consistent but cannot confirm the second sign independently.
Salut-ST1-jar-impression.context: ditch around tower ST1, Umm an-Nar period; contextual C14 2460-2145 cal BC (SU55), not a direct date
sources: Frenez, Degli Esposti, Méry, Kenoyer 2016, PSAS 46: 117-118 fig.10 (zenodo 5514184)

texts.object: steatite square stamp seal, boss on back
texts.scene: unicorn with standard (cult object) under head
texts.period: Period III, early Mature Harappan levels (layers 3-4 region; exact layer not given)
texts.reading_note: ~5 signs in top register; photo too low-resolution for a firm sign-by-sign transcription (brochure back cover). Needs a better image.
sources: ASI Excavation Branch II 2016, Binjor (4MSR) brochure, back cover
Manjul & Manjul 2021, Asokasri vol. I pp. 3-7 (text; plate 1.6 not in the upload)

texts.object: terracotta square seal with pierced boss, script only (3 signs)
texts.period: late Mature Harappan (late levels of Period III)
signs_W_tentative: two tall strokes with top ticks (W32 tall-2?)
human figure, arms slanting down (W90 family?)
texts.reading_note: Seal face shown; reading order on the impression is the mirror. Human-x-human 3-sign texts occur 3 times in the merged corpus; human signs normally sit after the jar W740 at text end (740-90).
sources: ASI 2016 brochure back cover; text p.7 'terracotta seal having only three Harappan letters'
